eyebrow: SOC Operations, SIEM & Log Analysis · Chapter 4
subtitle: Lesson 14 · Correlation Rules & Alert Logic

code:
RULE: Brute-force logon -> success
GROUP BY: user account

IF  5+ logon failures (group)
    WITHIN 10 minutes
AND 1 logon success (same group)
    after the failures, same window
THEN alert(severity=high)
caption: Same logic as Splunk SPL, Sentinel KQL, or any other SIEM's rule builder — just not tied to one syntax.

steps.label: GROUP BY
steps.sub: the grouping key — ties events into one pattern, e.g. same user account

steps.label: Success, same group
steps.sub: separates a real guess-and-land from unrelated typos

steps.label: alert(severity=high)
steps.sub: the action — what an analyst actually sees

code:
Fail Fail Fail Fail Fail Success
  -> matches: guess-and-land

Fail Success Fail Fail Fail Fail
  -> does NOT match: unrelated typos
caption: A sequence-aware rule checks what came before the success, not just how many events happened.

steps.label: Count-only rule
steps.sub: fires on both patterns above — too broad

steps.label: Sequence-aware rule
steps.sub: fires only when failures lead directly into the success

steps.label: Result
steps.sub: a rule aimed at real attacker behavior, not raw event volume
